Complaint Between XX/XX/year>, and XX/XX/year>, I initiated XXXX XXXX  remittance transfers through Abound using ACH debits from my XXXX checking account. The transfers were all sent to my own personal bank account in XXXX, not to a third party. 

The transaction details are as follows XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6100.00} ( including fees ) XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6100.00} XXXX XXXX  XX/XX/year> : {$6100.00} XXXX  XX/XX/year> : {$6000.00} XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6000.00} XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6000.00} XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6000.00} XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> : {$6000.00} The total amount debited from my bank account was approximately USD {$48000.00}. 

My first remittance through Abound had previously completed successfully after about XXXX days. Based on that successful experience, I initiated these additional transfers. 

Abound immediately withdrew the funds from my bank account. The application confirms that the funds were received by Abound. However, the transfers have not been completed. 

The transaction status initially displayed : Transfer delayed, but no cause for concern. Your money is safe & secure. This has been escalated internally and is being handled on priority. 

Some transactions now display estimated delivery dates, while others continue to show delayed processing. Despite these status messages, the funds have not been delivered to my bank account. 

Since the delays began, I have contacted Abounds customer support multiple times through email, as email is their only available customer support channel. Each time, I received only generic responses asking me to wait. The company has not provided a specific reason for the delays, has not requested any additional documentation, and has not provided a firm resolution date or offered a refund. 

These funds are urgently needed due to personal financial obligations, and the prolonged delay has caused significant financial hardship. 

I respectfully request that Abound : 1. Complete all pending remittance transfers immediately, or 2. Refund the full amount of all pending transactions to my original bank account immediately. 

I also request that Abound provide : * A written explanation for the delays. 
* Confirmation whether the transfers are under compliance or operational review. 
* A definitive timeline for resolution. 

I have retained screenshots of all transaction statuses, records showing the ACH debits from my bank account, and copies of my email communications with Abound, and I am prepared to provide them upon request.

narrative:
On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a call from XXXX from First Foundation Bank in XXXX XXXX XXXX  at XXXX. ( First Foundation Bank was recently acquired by XXXX XXXX  ) She informed me that there were several transactions made on my debit card from my checking account that appeared fraudulent and asked me to confirm the transactions. I told her I was at work and did not make any of the transactions she listed. I checked my wallet, and the debit card was still there ; so it wasn't lost or stolen. Somebody must have gotten a hold of my cards info, and used it to make these purchases. She immediately froze my debit card and asked me to come in to go over everything. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I went into the bank and XXXX showed me the transactions in question. Most of the transactions did not go through. Unfortunately, one transaction from XX/XX/XXXX, for {$990.00} from XXXX XXXX did go through. XXXX then helped me to file a fraud claim that same day, claim number XXXX. The money was provisionally credited back to my account. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I noticed while checking my account through the bank App, that the provisional credit of {$990.00} was reversed. The bank did not give me any notification prior to reversing the credit. I immediately went back to the bank and spoke to XXXX that same day. She looked up my account; and confirmed that they did not give me any notice prior to removing money from my account ; and that the fraud claim was denied. She printed out the bank 's paperwork from their investigation, and informed me that the fraud occurred at the XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX. She informed me that the next step was to submit a second claim and recommended filing a police report. I went home and reviewed the paperwork she had given me. I discovered that the bank has the original order from XXXX XXXX which says the shipping address where the merchandise was shipped. That information is redacted in the version they gave me ; but they should be able to see that the shipping address doesn't match my own address. I can see that the person who committed the fraud used my correct mailing address in the payment information. They also had my correct email address, and correct phone number. They also claim that there was an email verification ; but I've checked my email and there is nothing there from XXXX XXXX. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I called XXXX and informed her that I would like to do a second claim ; which she filed for me on XX/XX/XXXX. 
I filed a police report for this claim on XX/XX/XXXX with XXXX  XXXX from the XXXX XXXX Police Department, incident report # XXXX. I also noticed in the bank 's paperwork for the investigation that the XXXX address they list the transaction coming from does not match the IP address on my phone or work computer. These are the only devices I have access to ; which should show it was not possible to me to have made this transaction. On XX/XX/XXXX, I went back to the bank and gave the police report number and IP address information to XXXX ; who immediately faxed the new information to their fraud department. This purchase was also made on a day that I was at work in XXXXXXXX XXXX. My employer has the work records, and cameras verifying that I was at work that day making it impossible for me to have made the transaction. 
It has now been around XXXX  months since I reported the fraud, but the bank still has not credited the money back to my account. I am attaching all of the paperwork the bank has given me to this report.

The rule does not allow a bank or fintech program manager to delay opening the dispute internally and then use that later internal processing date as the legal start date.

The {$340.00} was only my remaining account balance returned to me by closure check after the account was closed. It was money already owed to me.
